reading.title: A Postcard from Cedar Cove
reading.purpose: Read a letter from a boy who just moved to a small town by the sea.
paras: Dear Cousin Hana, We finally unpacked our boxes! Our family moved to a rainy coastal region on the west edge of our continent. I miss our old street, yet I am starting to like it here.

We chose to settle in Cedar Cove. It is a quiet village where only a few hundred people live. The population is tiny next to the busy state capital where you live and where lawmakers meet. Every resident I meet waves when we walk past the mail room.

My best spot is the rocky harbor, a safe bay where boats tie up away from big waves. Right behind the water sits a steep hill. That landform blocks some of the ocean wind. From the top, I watch boats come in each morning.

On Saturdays, folks meet at the dock to trade goods. Mom swapped apple jam for fresh berries. I traded two comic books for a shell. Next month, write my name with a big capital C and come see us! Your cousin, Mateo.

choices: a steep rocky hill that blocks the ocean wind from blowing into town
a safe bay where boats stay away from waves
a busy dock market where families swap fresh berries and comic books
a small mail room near the main street of a quiet village
qs.why: Mateo describes the harbor as "a safe bay where boats tie up away from big waves."

qs.q: Which sentence shows that people in Cedar Cove are friendly to Mateo's family?
choices: We chose to settle in Cedar Cove.
The population is tiny next to the busy state capital where you live and where lawmakers meet.
Every resident I meet waves when we walk past the mail room.
On Saturdays, folks meet at the dock to trade goods.
qs.why: This sentence shows the friendly action of every resident waving to Mateo.

ev.text: Every resident I meet waves when we walk past the mail room.

qs.q: How is Hana's city different from Mateo's new home?
choices: Hana's city sits right next to a rocky ocean bay filled with small fishing boats.
Hana's city has a much bigger population than Mateo's village.
Hana's city has no mail room and no place for families to trade goods.
Hana's city is on a different continent far across the wide ocean.
qs.why: Mateo says his village's population is tiny next to the busy state capital where Hana lives.

qs.q: What is Mateo's letter mostly about?
choices: How to cook apple jam and collect painted shells along a rainy beach
Why lawmakers meet in a state capital instead of a small fishing town
What life and land are like in Mateo's new coastal village
How to draw a map of all seven continents on Earth for a class project
qs.why: Mateo describes the region, village, people, harbor, hills, and Saturday trading in his new home.

clues.text: where only a few hundred people live
a safe bay where boats tie up away from big waves
swapped apple jam for fresh berries
